To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
vitamin D supplementation does not increase serum TT levels in healthy middle-aged men.
in men with low baseline testosterone levels, 12 weeks of vitamin D supplementation did not increase testosterone levels.
vitamin D treatment had no significant effect on serum total testosterone (primary endpoint) and on the remaining secondary endpoint variables.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of vitamin D on testosterone levels in men with vitamin D deficiency and low testosterone levels.
the effects of vitamin D supplementation in men.
the question of whether vitamin D supplementation is effective in the treatment of hypogonadal men.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
vitamin D has no effect on androgen levels in healthy men.
vitamin D supplementation has no effect on TT levels in men with subnormal levels at baseline.
the effects of vitamin D treatment on serum testosterone levels are not yet fully understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
vitamin D is not a hormone that regulates androgen levels in healthy men.
vitamin D is not a treatment option to increase testosterone levels in men.
vitamin D does not seem to play an important role in androgen metabolism in middle-aged men with low testosterone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the vitamin D status is not a major determinant of androgen levels.
vitamin D supplementation does not seem to have a significant effect on androgens and that TT levels should be evaluated in the context of other risk factors for hypogonadism.
the effect of vitamin D on androgen status is unlikely to be clinically relevant.
